sources: Koch 2006, s.v. 'wild man in Celtic legend'
text: The wild man is a figure of Celtic legend. He first appears as a king or poet. A terrible defeat in battle drives him mad. He flees into the wild wood. There he lives a solitary life like an animal. Myrddin, later known as Merlin, is the finest example. Suíbne Geilt offers the Irish form of the tale. Lailoken supplies a third version in northern Britain. The wild man gains prophecy in his exile. His hardened body and his frenzy separate him from sound men.

okr.objective: Describe the Celtic wild man and his famous examples.
